pillar_reactions.evidence: Pre-sold on the modality before the pillar was even delivered — 'whenever there is a kettlebell complex or stuff where I get to slam a hammer down or flip a tire, those were always the workouts that I was most engaged in'. When the mobility half landed he tied it directly to his own MRI findings and answered the philosophy with 'I like that'. This is the pillar carrying the whole call.

Rep pre-emptively demoted it — 'that's going to be probably the least important thing out of the three for you' — and the prospect agreed without question, having already said 'I would say pretty good' about food quality and 'tracking it helps me build the right awareness'. No pushback, no curiosity either.

The video-form-review and daily tick mechanic was understood and mapped onto prior experience: 'when I was on active duty we had strength coaches... it was a relatively similar process. The only difference was that they could be there and provide immediate feedback on form... but I'm very comfortable with the asynchronous feedback type of thing.'

anchors.raw: I was using Built by Science, which is an app that does like nutrition tracking and like custom workouts based on what equipment you have
anchors.note: An app-priced substitute that demonstrably delivered his headline result — 24 lb of weight loss. He rejected it on engagement, not on efficacy, so the $6,000 has to justify itself against something that already worked for the outcome his wife will care about.

anchors.raw: I think my fallback would be Primal University if she is just like, we cannot spend 6K
anchors.competitor: Primal University (Primal Instinct's own self-guided product)
anchors.note: The company's own lower-priced product is the named alternative to a $6,000 close, and the prospect already has an email about it. The rep conceded ground on it — 'I find it hard to upsell people at a Primal University' — and separated the two only on the medical condition. If this recurs at scale the self-guided product is cannibalising the high-ticket close.

anchors.raw: The VA sent me to a chiropractor and that was fantastic... but the VA only covered 12 appointments
anchors.note: A veteran's baseline expectation is that body work is a covered benefit at zero marginal cost. Minor as an anchor but relevant to a military-heavy lead source.

anchors.raw: I think she will be skeptical for 6k
anchors.note: The number in the household's head is whatever Lauren will tolerate, not what Parker will. The rep's response was to shrink the instalment, plus an unsolicited tax write-off framing to make it feel 'nearly free' — both of which concede that $6,000 is the problem rather than reframing the value.

unmet_demand.want: Training variety beyond kettlebells — sledgehammer work, tire flips, gymnastic rings — because repetition is the exact reason every previous programme failed for him
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme is explicitly the kettlebell/nutrition/mobility trifecta. The rep answered variety with 'everything's tailored' rather than saying whether the other implements he named are actually programmed.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that loaded overhead work is safe for a documented cervical compression and bilateral shoulder impingement
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Addressed as a coaching-technique matter ('the first month is all about technique and a low weight') rather than as a clinical question. No clearance pathway exists in the offer, so a prospect who wanted medical reassurance could not be given one.

unmet_demand.want: Learning to write his own programming so he is not dependent on a coach — the gap he named from 14 years of military training
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Actually well served and well answered — 'you know how to write your own plans... we want to educate you up to that point'. Recorded because it is the strongest value hook on the call and the only one that landed as a decision reason.
